chapter: Bands, lake camps and early players
title: Bucking the white bands at the lake camps and the Camellia boat
summary: Glass recalls bucking with Gallaty, Philly Ray and Sharkey at Milneburg camps, the Camellia boat and excursion train, and how Black and white neighbors once got along.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Yeah. They had Buck Vanville's band there for years. Yeah. The Philly Red. You remember Philly Red? Yeah. You remember Philly Red? Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.

Yeah. Yeah. I heard of them. Yeah. Yeah. I heard of them. Phil and Ray, Bill Gallaty. Mm-hmm. All them fellas used to, we used to buck together on the lake. Which Bill Gallaty? Bill Gallaty, he used to play bass.
Oh yeah, not the young man today that plays trumpet. Yeah.

One played trumpet and one used to play the bass. And Philly Ray used to play bass. We used to get on the lake and buck out there. The camps would be right there, side and side. We used to get there and blow at each other. Dixon Land.
You're talking about humpback Gallaty though. Yeah.

The Dixon Land man. That's why we played. They used to play the music that we play now. Yeah. And we'd buck on the lake every Sunday. We'd go out there on a Saturday night. That's where the money stopped. Start the raise and you know the price.
Is that the area they used to call Meilenburg? The Meilenburg.

Meilenburg. Meilenburg. Yeah. More Road, we'd be out there playing for More Road and then we'd be in all them camp playing across from each other. We used to buck. Bill Gallaty, he ain't long died. He old. All of them dying. Philly Ray. Old timers, you know. Sharky, he left. Sharky used to be out there. We used to be, me and Sharky used to talk about you. Sharky used to say, Glass, you still living you old rascal. We used to be, oh, me and Sharky, that'd be like that. Well you used to mix it up? Yeah, we used to buck out there on the lake. Yeah. Yeah, we used to buck out there. The camp, this camp here, we'd be right there. We'd be blowing at each other. Yeah, we used to play that music out there. Every sudden we'd go on the boat and play, the camellial. Yeah, the boat used to go across the lake. across the lake. They called it the Camellia. Did it go along the canal and get the lake? It'd go across, it'd bring you across the lake and it'd come back in the evening and trip. The Camellia boat. Where did it leave from? It leave from right out there on the wharf by Littlefield Street there. The train would go out on the wharf, a punching train. She'd roll right on out to the wharf and get off the hood. End of the wharf. And that little excursion train would go out there? She'd be clear on, she'd leave at the junction up there. Littlefield and the kid up there. But that's where the punching train used to be. That she'd back up and come back and go to Millen Boy. And that's where we'd get that train and go out there and flip. Sometimes we'd be out there all night on a Saturday and Sunday we'd be out there on picnets, you know. They'd have them in camp. Play all night and all day out there. We'd be bucking. The white band and the colored band. They were always like that. They didn't have that pulling in the hall like they were doing, you know. They was all like that. They'd come up that way. The colored would stay next door to you, they'd hand you something to dinner over there. My grandmother would hand the white people something over there. That's the way they got along, long time ago. They didn't, they didn't, they didn't pull in the hall. They'd pull in the hall and this come up at the time of the young race. It wasn't like that. They'd give you anything they had. And if you were sick they'd come in that house and stay there with you because some of your people would come. They'd have to mind you. And they'd wash you. They'd have to wash you. They used to come and help to wash the colored people when they died, the women. They'd come and help you. So this would change what I was used to that, you see. And I'm a little tired down now because everything is changed now. Yes, it must be very different. Yeah. They just got you that you could go anywhere. So they'd give you anything you had.
